cohort: The study included 46 women, comprising 11 with placental permeability dysfunction (PE, PP, PA, or PMD) and 35 controls without such complications.
finding: The prevalence rate of occult fetomaternal hemorrhage was significantly higher in women with placental complications (36%) compared to controls (2.9%).
cross-section timing: Antenatal and postnatal blood samples were obtained from participants.
